core_obligations: Set up the framework lemma with its assumptions (1) and (2) from the cited locality lemma; state the goal: given the cartesian square with Z' \to Z surjective flat of affines and X' \to Z' an open immersion, show X \to Z is an open immersion (proof lines 1723-1730).

Identify |X'| with an open U' \subset Z' satisfying pr_0^{-1}(U') = pr_1^{-1}(U') on Z' \times_Z Z', and descend it to an open U \subset Z with X' = (Z' \to Z)^{-1}(U) via the cited Descent lemma on opens along fpqc coverings (proof lines 1732-1740).

Use the fpqc sheaf condition for X to promote the section U' \to X' \to X to a morphism U \to X over \mathcal{U} = {U' \to U}, then prove the map of sheaves U \to X is bijective by the pointwise factorization argument (every T-valued point of X factors through U), concluding the proof (proof lines 1742-1760).
proof_roadmap: Feed the locality assumptions into the framework lemma.
Descend the open subset along the fpqc covering.
Glue via the sheaf condition and verify bijectivity on T-valued points.
difficulty_reason: The proof goes through the framework lemma (assumptions from the cited immersion locality lemma), then descends the open itself: |X'| \subset |Z'| corresponds to an open U' \subset Z' with pr_0^{-1}(U') = pr_1^{-1}(U'), so fppc-style descent of opens (cited Descent lemma) produces an open U \subset Z with X' the pullback; the fpqc sheaf condition for X (cited proposition) turns the section U' \to X' \to X into a morphism U \to X over the covering; finally the pointwise factorization argument shows the map of sheaves U \to X is bijective, so X \to Z is an open immersion. The descent of the open plus the sheaf-level bijection are the substance.
